our_argument_summary: The dome's 'Southern Distance Quadratic' law (ratio = 0.00131·lat² + 0.06828·lat + 1.06719, R²=0.7874) plus its V50.6 H(r) exponential firmament coordinate conversion are two generations of post-hoc projection calibration fitted against a small city-pair sample, with mean 5.2% error requiring at least four free parameters — vs standard spherical geodesy (Vincenty/Karney on WGS84) at sub-millimetre precision with two parameters. Verdict: Misleading.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: The quadratic latitude-dependent distortion is the azimuthal equidistant projection signature — standard cartography, published for centuries. V50.6 H(r) with a solved radial coordinate r·tan(polaris_elev)=H(r) is a calibrated latitude-to-radius map that back-solves for whatever disc radius makes planar trig approximate spherical trig — again, standard projection theory. Dome relabels 'projection distortion' as 'dome discovery.'
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: raw-text/02-wins.txt line 135 documents the sequence: v22 circular disc failed on southern/cross-equator distances; WIN-027 quadratic and WIN-030 ellipse were fitted specifically to patch that failure; V12 H(r)+EW angular scale further reduced mean error from ~40% to 5.2%. Each step is a fitted correction after the previous geometry failed — the textbook post-hoc adjustment pattern.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: No derivation from the dome parameters (disc_radius, firmament_height, sun/moon altitude) yields the quadratic coefficients or H(r) parameters. The coefficients are regression outputs against globe-derived (WGS84) distances. r_eq=14,105 km, H₀=8,537, λ=8,619, EW=0.9941 are all fit constants, not derived quantities.

holes_found.description: The 'Scale comparison and the long-haul kill' paragraph claims Sydney (~34°S) and Santiago (~33.5°S) 'sit near the southern edge at r ≈ 16,000 km from centre' and that the planar chord 'exceeds ~30,000 km, almost three times the globe great-circle distance.' Both numbers are wrong under the V50.6 model the paragraph purports to critique. Under V50.6 r·tan(polaris_elevation)=H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619), Sydney at lat=−33.86° maps to r ≈ 6,198 km, Santiago at lat=−33.45° to r ≈ 6,255 km (not 16,000 km — 16,000 km corresponds to |lat|≈54°, not 34°). With EW-scaled Δθ=138.15°·0.9941=137.33°, the V50.6 planar chord is √(6198²+6255²−2·6198·6255·cos137.33°) ≈ 11,600 km, within ~3% of the WGS84 great-circle 11,349 km. Under the older V9 naïve (90−lat)·111.1 mapping, r ≈ 13,779 km (Sydney) / 13,716 km (Santiago), giving a chord ≈ 25,600 km — also nowhere near 30,000 km, and clearly '2.26×' not 'almost three times'. A dome defender can compute either number in 30 seconds and reverse the 'kill shot' on our own page. The underlying critique (V50.6 is a projection calibration whose out-of-sample generalization is untested) remains valid, but this specific numerical example does the opposite of what it advertises — it demonstrates that V50.6 CAN reproduce Sydney–Santiago within a few percent, precisely because r(lat) is calibrated to do so.
holes_found.recommendation: Rewrite the 'Scale comparison and the long-haul kill' paragraph. Drop the incorrect r≈16,000/chord>30,000 example. Replace with the correct in-sample vs out-of-sample framing: V50.6 achieves 5.2% mean error BY DESIGN on the 19 pairs it was fit against (nothing is being predicted — cities are placed at whatever r(lat) makes the answer come out right); the model reports no cross-validation, no held-out pair test, no reported worst-case beyond the curated 'V9 89% → V50.6 0.0% Oslo-Stockholm' single win. The proper long-haul kill is not 'the chord is too big' (V50.6 calibrates it) but 'V50.6 has zero out-of-sample validation — the 5.2% mean is training-set fit, not predictive accuracy.' Alternatively, keep a distance example but pick one where V50.6 is DOCUMENTED to fail — the 'Worst case: V9 89% Oslo-Stockholm → V50.6 0.0%' presentation on the dome page implies V50.6 has NO acknowledged worst case in its training set; anything not on the 19-pair list is unknown-unknown territory, and any transhemispheric pair not on the list becomes the empirical test. Consider a Cape Town–Perth or Buenos Aires–Cape Town pair (both trans-southern-hemisphere, plausibly outside the 19-pair training set).

stronger_arguments.description: The generalization argument is the real kill. V50.6's 5.2% is reported as 'Mean distance error' on the training set (raw-text/05-model.txt line 48: 'V9 ~40% → V50.6 5.2%'). No out-of-sample or held-out pair test is described. The '19 city pairs tested' is the training set, and per raw-text line 50 the 'worst case' is presented as Oslo-Stockholm going V9 89% → V50.6 0.0% — the DOME's own worst case is a case where V50.6 gets a perfect score on a pair its parameters were fit against. Standard machine-learning practice puts no weight on training-set fit for predictive accuracy claims; the dome's presentation IS the kill shot if we frame it that way.
sources: Vincenty (1975) Survey Review 23(176):88 for the two-parameter globe baseline

stronger_arguments.description: The 'r_eq = 14,105 km equatorial ring' parameter is separately vulnerable. Standard cartographic projections (azimuthal equidistant, gnomonic, stereographic) get by with zero latitude-dependent free constants. r_eq is a fourth free parameter tuned to make the V50.6 map close smoothly across the equator. A defender who accepts 'projections need calibration' cannot then claim the calibration reveals structure — every well-known map projection is a two-parameter (semi-major axis, flattening) map of the SAME globe.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome has correctly identified something real: any azimuthal projection of a sphere onto a flat disc will produce systematic, latitude-dependent distance distortions with roughly quadratic character in lat, and the quadratic coefficients (0.00131·lat² + 0.06828·lat + 1.06719) are the numerical signature of exactly that projection distortion (cited in the review's own detail_evidence, wins.json id=027 first paragraph). The V50.6 H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) km calibration is a legitimate mathematical response to the projection distortion problem — it's the same class of solution any calibrated projection uses (raw-text/05-model.txt lines 16, 33).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Being right about the DISTORTION pattern doesn't save the dome's CAUSAL claim. Standard cartography (Vincenty 1975 Survey Review 23(176):88, Karney 2013 arxiv:1109.4448 'Algorithms for geodesics') derives the distortion from a sphere→plane projection using two constants and achieves sub-millimetre absolute accuracy globally without any latitude-dependent free parameters. The dome uses four fitted free parameters (H₀=8,537, λ=8,619, EW angular scale 0.9941, r_eq=14,105 km per raw-text/05-model.txt lines 16, 37, 57 and WIN-057) and still reports 5.2% mean error on 19 in-sample pairs. Recovering the projection signature confirms the sphere; assigning it to a physical dome geometry is post-hoc renaming, not new physics.

advocate_mode.best_defense: The strongest dome-defender attack post-c6 patch is the internal numerical error in the 'Scale comparison and the long-haul kill' paragraph: 'You claim Sydney and Santiago sit at r ≈ 16,000 km from the disc centre and that the planar chord between them exceeds 30,000 km. Under my own V50.6 model — H(r) = 8537·exp(−r/8619), r solving r·tan(polaris_elevation) = H(r) — Sydney at lat = −33.86° maps to r ≈ 6,200 km, and the planar chord to Santiago at lat = −33.45° is ~11,600 km, matching your own quoted great-circle 11,338 km within 3%. Your kill shot fails against the very model you claim to be critiquing. If you cannot compute r(lat) from my equations before publishing a debunk, why should any reader trust your other quantitative claims?' This is the kind of specific numerical reversal that plays well on comment sections and social-media threads and can be verified in 30 seconds by anyone with a calculator. It does NOT flip the Misleading verdict (the post-hoc calibration critique, the 5.2% mean on 19 in-sample pairs, and the four-free-parameter framing remain untouched), but it discredits a decisive-sounding paragraph and gives the defender a rhetorical win.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Do the major-severity rewrite above BEFORE the dome author (who is known to read the review per the CLAUDE.md author-contact record) or any AI-assisted defender surfaces this. The rewrite is a scoped patch to one paragraph; the surrounding argument (post-hoc, four parameters, no derivation from dome geometry, 5.2% mean is training-set fit) all survives unchanged. The out-of-sample framing is stronger than the chord-arithmetic framing anyway, so the rewrite is a net argument-quality improvement, not just a defensive edit.

quantitative_verification.computations: Python haversine for the great-circle. Bisection solve of r·tan(|lat|)=8537·exp(−r/8619) for both cities. Planar chord via law of cosines with EW-angular-scaled Δθ. Adjusted R² via standard formula 1−(1−R²)(n−1)/(n−k−1). Crossref API for Vincenty DOI; direct fetch for Karney arxiv title.

deeper_analysis: The c6 review left WIN-027 in a clean state modulo one sub-meter/sub-millimetre tldr_verdict inconsistency, which has since been patched (evidenced by tldr_verdict length growing from 317 to 322 chars, consistent with 'sub-meter'→'sub-millimetre'). Between c6 (2026-04-16) and this c7 spot-check (2026-07-02), the fingerprint on all other fields is unchanged — the text has been stable for ~11 weeks. That stability made this a legitimate spot-check target: content that has escaped scrutiny for a season and might carry latent errors nobody re-verified. The c7 fresh-eyes read surfaced two errors that c6 did not flag: (1) a quantitative reversal of the 'long-haul kill' paragraph under the V50.6 model it critiques, and (2) a code_analysis.monitoring tag mismatch against the live monitor.py (which the c6 review only checked structurally, not by domain enumeration). The pattern — 'this section has been unchallenged for months and now someone has computed a specific counter-number' — is exactly the failure mode spot-checks exist to catch. Neither finding flips the Misleading verdict; both need patching before the dome-defender-with-a-calculator scenario surfaces.
